articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Attican Traverse: Krogan Team Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

War Assets: (note that the middle asset is based on your actions in Mass Effect 2, while the other two assets are mutually exclusive) Aralakh Company (25 TMS) Tap to Reveal (25 TMS) Tap to Reveal (100 TMS)

Prerequisite : Complete " Priority: Sur’Kesh "

Location : Ninmah Cluster - Mulla Xul - Utukku

While this Mission is unlocked immediately after you complete " Priority: Sur'Kesh ", you'll have been asked by your Krogan Leader (either Wrex or Wreav) to meet them in the War Room to discuss the matter. One of their teams was scouting past the old Rachni Relay and immediately went missing. Shepard is to meet with Urdnot's best unit, Aralakh Company, and investigate.

To begin, head to the Ninmah Cluster and wander into the Mulla Xul system. It’ll take you to Utukku, the purported location of the missing krogan scouts.

Squad Tactics: Garrus is a great choice if you have him for his Armor-Piercing Ammo and Proximity Mine powers, and focus on sniper rifles. Javik is also a good choice if you have him thanks to his biotic abilities, including a grenade of his own. If you don't have Javik, Kaidan or Liara's biotics are almost as useful. If you save this Mission until after " Priority: Perseus Veil " (which we don't recommend), Tali is a good option if available for her Defense Drone power.

Garrus is a great choice if you have him for his Armor-Piercing Ammo and Proximity Mine powers, and focus on sniper rifles.

Javik is also a good choice if you have him thanks to his biotic abilities, including a grenade of his own.

If you don't have Javik, Kaidan or Liara's biotics are almost as useful.

If you save this Mission until after " Priority: Perseus Veil " (which we don't recommend), Tali is a good option if available for her Defense Drone power.

Unique Dialogue: Javik is a good choice if you have him, as he has some unique insight regarding the history the enemy you'll be facing here. Garrus will have some friendly relations with the leader of Aralakh Company, if they survived Mass Effect 2.

Garrus will have some friendly relations with the leader of Aralakh Company, if they survived Mass Effect 2.

Shepard's Loadout: If you have the From Ashes DLC, the Particle Rifle is a very good choice for its replenishing ammo. You can use it to clear out obstacles, letting you save M-451 Firestorm ammo for enemies, at least on easier difficulties. The wide open spaces of this level make Sniper Rifles very useful here. Shotguns of course also come in handy for the Husks you'll be fighting in this Mission.

If you have the From Ashes DLC, the Particle Rifle is a very good choice for its replenishing ammo. You can use it to clear out obstacles, letting you save M-451 Firestorm ammo for enemies, at least on easier difficulties.

The wide open spaces of this level make Sniper Rifles very useful here.

Shotguns of course also come in handy for the Husks you'll be fighting in this Mission.

After some scenes discussing the situation in the shuttle, you'll land and meet with the leader of Aralakh Company. Normally this will be a character named Urdnot Dagg, but if Grunt was awakened in Mass Effect 2 and survived the Suicide Mission, then he'll be the Company Leader! He'll even note if you completed his Loyalty Mission, which will be important later...

You can also get some Morality Points here. The wording will differ depending on who the Company Leader is, but in either way the upper-right option awards +2 Paragon Points , while the lower-right option awards +2 Renegade Points .

Either way, take the Company Leader's advice and explore the area for goodies.

M-300 Claymore - After assuming control of Shepard, head into the building on your left to pick up this weapon. It'll be on the bed directly across from the entryway.

Pistol High Caliber Barrel - In the same building as the M-300 Claymore, you’ll find it sitting atop a bed further into the building.

Spare Parts - 1,625 credits. Also inside the building, on some PC tower-like boxes near the entryway.

The M-300 Claymore 's Clayme to Fayme is having the single most powerful shot of any weapon in the entire game, and is especially good on Shields. However it's extremely heavy, can only fire one shot per reload, and fires pellets rather than a slug. Only use this if you are willing to work around these issues.

Continue down the hill to find the lower part of the camp, teetering on the edge of the cliff. There's more goodies here:

SMG High Caliber Barrel - In the back of the left-hand building, in the same room as a Weapon Bench.

Spare Parts - 875 credits. On the right-hand side of the building with the SMG High Caliber Barrel. It'll be on some PC towers, behind a large crate and a pair of Krogan.

Outside the right-hand building, you'll find the Aralakh Company Leader. You should talk to them now to learn more about their team, especially if the Leader is Grunt: he'll fill you in on what he's been up to since Mass Effect 2.

Now head into the building the Company leader is standing outside of. Unfortunately the weight of Shepard and their squad is enough to cause the building to crash down to the bottom of the hole, separating you from Aralakh Company.

Head forward into the caves, and you'll spot the body of a scout. Take the Company leader's suggestion and grab his weapon: an M-451 Firestorm .

Formerly a DLC Heavy Weapon in Mass Effect 2, the M-451 Firestorm is a flamethrower that deals a good amount of damage. It works much like the Particle Rifle from the From Ashes DLC in that it gets a big damage boost after a second of sustained fire. It's short range (and quirk that it can only hit a single target) means it's primarily useful for clearing webbing and egg sacks here on Mulla Xul.

Pick up the Firestorm weapon and use it to burn away the webbing blocking the tunnel entrance in front of you. It's VERY effective! Note that if you switch weapons, you will simply drop the Firestorm at your feet, allowing you to pick it up again.

You'll enter a tunnel that’s completely draped in darkness. With only a flashlight in front of you, you’ll need to navigate the darkness and destroy any obstacles, such as the Spore Pods. Spore Pods are biomechanical egg sacks that burst when you get too close to them, dealing damage.

However, if you deal some light damage to them, they'll explode after a few seconds, letting you safely destroy them!

Unfortunately the Firestorm isn't as good on Spore Pods as it is are on the Webbing. If you run out of juice on your Firestorm, there are others dotted about various Krogan corpses as you venture inward: one will be behind a wall of Webbing at the second cluster of Spore Pods.

Before dropping into the sunlit open area, look for a Reaper-looking device on the rocks straight ahead. This is a Barrier Engine, and they're incredibly annoying! Destroying this now will greatly ease the upcoming fight.

As soon as you leave the pitch black darkness of the tunnel, you'll run headfirst into a myriad of Husks , and a band new enemy type called Ravagers . Ravagers boast a rock hard armored exoskeleton, and a pair of long-range cannons that WILL punish you if you stay out in the open. Making matters worse, their pink tumors will release little Swarmers , as well as a pool of acid that damages Shepard if they walk over it.

Also in this area is a piece of Reaper tech called a Barrier Engine. This works similarly to Cerberus' Shield Pylons, only here they add a layer of biotic Barriers. Garrus' Armor-Piercing Ammo works good on Barriers, but the better solution is to destroy the Barrier Engine itself.

Shotgun Shredder Mod - Once the battle is over, return to where Shepard dropped in here from and face the way forward. Head left to find a dead Krogan with this mod next to him.

With the presence of Rachni confirmed, you’re now tasked with finding the nest and eradicating the source. Slog through the thick cluster of Spore Nodes (using the View Prompt as you go) to eventually come across an important-looking Reaper Node. While it's protected by a Barrier, the nearby Firestorm will work very well on it, and the metal wall will recede so you can continue.

Unfortunately, you'll encounter a cave-in, meaning you can't leave here from the way you came.

You'll now be back to navigating the quiet dark of the tunnels. There's two ways forward, an elevated path, and a lower waterlogged path, which soon meet back up again. We prefer taking the left-hand waterlogged path because it's easier to tell when it meets up with the elevated path.

Reaper Tech - 3,750 credits. Where the two paths meet back up, look left to spot some Webbing. Destroy it to find this at the back wall.

Continue forwards a bit, and you'll be attacked by a lone Husk as you enter the next chamber.

Krogan Corpse - After killing the Husk, you'll spot two more Webbing walls on the left-hand wall. Destroy the closer one to find a Krogan Corpse behind it: Examine it to learn that he left a dying note. The starts the " Citadel: Krogan Dying Message " Side Mission, which you can hand in on the Citadel.

The drop up ahead is yet another spot where you can pre-emptively shoot out a Barrier Engine on the rocks up ahead. Make sure to do it so the next fight can go a bit more smoothly! There'll be a second Barrier Engine ahead on the left you can similarly take out early.

In the next area, your squad mates sense that imminent danger is mere moments away -- and they’re right. Husks, Cannibals and Ravagers start flooding out and attack. Be sure to first eliminate the Barrier Engines to prevent the enemies from being fortified with a Barrier that makes them tougher to kill. Many more enemies abound, which, as your squad mates point out, indicates your ever closer proximity to the nest.

Shotgun Spare Ammo - At the location of the second Barrier Engine, follow the left-hand wall forwards to find this at the top of the slope, next to a krogan corpse.

You'll then go down a drop, where the game will autosave and you'll get another update from Grunt.

Reaper Tech - 3,125 credits. After dropping down the ledge, clear out the Gestation Pods on your left to find this behind them.

Continue heading forward through the new Gestation Pods (which not only explode, but spawn Swarmers if you get too close), but keep an eye out on the left-hand wall for another Firestorm next to a Krogan Corpse. It'll help destroying the Pods if you don't have a Particle Rifle on you.

Ariake Technologies Shoulder Guard - After picking up the Firestorm described above, you'll jump across a gap to a waterlogged area. Up ahead is a ramp next to a waterfall: here will be this mod next to yet another krogan corpse.

Continue forward and you'll eventually be able to spot Aralakh Company on the right-hand side with a View Prompt. Their leader will inform you that they're blocked, so you'll have to solve that for them. Continue onwards, destroy the webbing, then drop down to where the Reaper Node is to help out Aralakh Company.

After the cutscene is over, you can grab the last items of the level:

Med Kit - 50 XP. Directly ahead of you after the cutscene, next to a krogan corpse.

Pistol Piercing Mod - Next to Med Kit described above.

Reaper Tech - 3,125 credits. At the start of the next tunnel, look right to spot a cluster of Gestation Pods. Destroy them to find this in the right-hand corner.

Examine the narrow passage and continue deeper into the Rachni’s central chamber. As soon as Shepard enters, impregnable, metal Reaper walls rise up and block your path. To progress, look up and to the left to spot the Power Node: destroy it to lower one side of the barricade... but you’ll have much resistance to contend with.

The goal is to keep fighting your way and disabling Reaper Nodes until you can reach the core node, all while fighting Reaper forces, including plenty of Ravagers and Husks. Keep an eye out for any Firestorms near the Reaper Nodes that you can use to help with the fighting, as well as Barrier Nodes that bolster their defenses.

After destroying the third Reaper Node in the area, you'll then meet the unwitting source of the Ravagers and Swarmers...

...but who exactly it is depends on your actions in Mass Effect 1:

If you spared the Rachni Queen , it will be her, having been captured by the Reapers and forced to breed the Ravagers and Swarmers for their army.

If you killed the Rachni Queen, in her place will be the Rachni Breeder , who outright states she isn't a queen, and that she may be able to control her future children.

Either one will claim to hate the Reapers and offer to assist Shepard's fight against them, however the Breeder will be much more... unstable about it. You can get some Morality Points here, but the wording differs on who it is you're talking to:

Pick "It's over now" / "The Reapers are gone" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "You're a puppet" / "You're a danger" for +2 Renegade Points .

After some more discussion with the Rachni, the leader of Aralakh Company then calls and makes clear that if Shepard stays any longer, the company will die. You'll have to make the difficult choice between the Rachni, or Aralakh Company:

If you choose to leave the Rachni to die, you'll gain Aralakh Company as a War Asset for 25 TMS, at the expense of the Rachni's aid.

If you choose to spare the Rachni, you'll gain Rachni Workers as a War Asset worth 100 TMS, at the expense of Aralakh Company. HOWEVER, if your Rachni is the Rachni Breeder, then Tap to Reveal .

HOWEVER, if your Rachni is the Rachni Breeder, then Tap to Reveal .

Whichever one you choose, you'll now make a mad escape out of the tunnels, and the Aralakh Company leader will offer to hold them off. Here's the possible outcomes for this finale:

If the Company Leader is Urdnot Dagg, he will always die at the end of the Mission.

If the Company Leader if Grunt, his survival depends on if you completed his Loyalty Mission, " Grunt: Rite of Passage ", in Mass Effect 2: If you completed his Loyalty Mission, Grunt will survive and meet up with Shepard at the shuttle. Grunt is considered his own separate War Asset from Aralakh Company, and is worth 25 TMS. If you didn't complete his Loyalty Mission, Grunt will die, and Shepard departs without him.

If you completed his Loyalty Mission, Grunt will survive and meet up with Shepard at the shuttle. Grunt is considered his own separate War Asset from Aralakh Company, and is worth 25 TMS.

If you didn't complete his Loyalty Mission, Grunt will die, and Shepard departs without him.

After debriefing Admiral Hackett on your choices on Mulla Xull, you'll do the same with your Krogan Leader. You can get some Morality Points here:

If Wrex is the Krogan Leader... Pick "It's over now" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "It wasn't pretty" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "It's over now" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "It wasn't pretty" for +2 Renegade Points .

If Wreav is the Krogan Leader and you opted to save the Rachni on Utukku... Pick "Excuse me?" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "You're a coward" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "Excuse me?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "You're a coward" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll get +5 Reputation and +5 Renegade Points for completing the Mission either way.

If this was the first main Mission you completed after " Priority: Sur'Kesh ", you'll now be approached by your STG Doctor saying he's developed a cure. You can get up to +4 Paragon Points or +4 Renegade Points depending on your choices, and unlock " Priority: Tuchanka " too! You still have total freedom to ignore it, however.

Now it's time to do the Normandy rounds:

CIC - Talk to Anderson in the Vid Comm room ( +2 Reputation ), Primarch Victus, your Krogan Leader for a new closing comment, Traynor to pick up " N7: Cerberus Abductions ", Joker and EDI.

Crew Deck - Pop by Garrus in the Port Observation deck, Chakwas and Adams in the Crew Quarters, Liara ( +2 Reputation and the Warp Bonus Power), her Broker terminal, overhear Mordin's song in the Med Bay, and ask your STG Doctor about "The Shroud".

Engineering - Talk to Javik, pass by Gabby and Ken (and talk to Ken), and swing by Allers.

articles.body:
Fencing Lessons Is a Side Quest in Novigrad with suggested level 12. This quest becomes available after Broken Flowers , if you agree to give Rosa more lessons, and it's a rather straightforward one in comparison to other Novigrad Side Quests.

To help you complete the Side Quest quickly, here's IGN's complete guide to Fencing Lessons, including the various options you'll have on offer when dealing with the duo of thugs at the very end.

You'll need to finish Broken Flowers before you can start this Side Quest. Speaking to Rosa during Broken Flowers will reveal that she wants fencing lessons, and if you agree, you'll be invited back to her estate the following day.

At Rosa's home, you'll be told that she's not actually home, and is instead on a walk with her bodyguard in the city. You'll need to head out and find her in the south east area of the city, near the water.

Rosa will request to fight with real swords, sending her bodyguard away. As you might imagine, there isn't much of a threat here, and you'll be able to beat her quickly with simple strikes.

After bringing Rosa's health down a significant amount, she'll order Geralt to turn around so she can readjust her corset. After complying, Geralt will turn back around to see that Rosa has slipped away.

Use your Witcher Senses to track Rosa to the Seven Cats Inn.

You will find two thugs harassing Rosa in the Inn. You'll be able to decide how you want to deal with them. You can use Axii, pay them off, or simply kill them. This won't change your final Side Quest reward.

When the thugs have been dealt with, a very unhappy Rosa will go home, wrapping up the Side Quest.

There isn't much of a reward on offer here; you'll be able to nab 25 x experience when you wrap up this Side Quest.

articles.body:
Contract: The White Lady is a Novigrad Side Quest . It has a suggested level of 16, and has a heavy, emotional story at its core. Some Side Quests simply require you to kill a monster and move on -- this one features a monster, but there's more to it than meets the eye.

To help you prepare for the combat encounter and complete the Side Quest, here's IGN's complete guide to Contract: The White Lady, including where to start the Contract and what you'll need to bring.

This Side Quest can be started by picking up the notice paper reading Contract: The White Lady off the notice board in the refugee district of the outskirts of Novigrad.

The Contract will guide you to a widow named Helma, who will tell you more about the monster that's plaguing the townsfolk -- it's some kind of Wraith, apparently. She can be found to the south of the area.

Four townspeople went to defeat the Wraith, but when you arrive at the designated crime scene and investigate using your Witcher Senses, you'll only see three bodies.

After examining the bodies, Geralt will determine that The White Lady is a Noonwraith .

Near the dead bodies, there will be some tracks leading away from the other bodies. Use your Witcher Senses and follow the tracks. The tracks lead to a broken tower and you will be led, in turn, to the cellar via a blood trail.

Head back to Helma to find something to draw the Noonwraith out. After talking to the widow, she will give you a dagger. Seemingly, the Noonwraith is a woman who took her life to avoid an arranged marriage, and the dagger was a betrothal gift.

Head back to the campsite which is near the dead bodies. Be sure to use your Specter Oil beforehand if you haven't already, and wait until it's daytime for the Noonwraith to appear if it isn't already. Throw the dagger into the fire when you're ready to fight.

Much like other Wraiths in the game, this Noonwraith is vulnerable to both Specter Oil and Yrden. You'll need to use Yrden to make sure that the beast is strikable, and dodge her attacks in the meanwhile.

When the Noonwraith falls, loot the body to claim a Noonwraith Trophy and the Silver Sword Deithwen, then head back to the quest-giver to turn in the Side Quest and claim your final reward.

Turning in this Side Quest will net you your negotiated fee, along with 260 x experience.

articles.title: Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk is a Novigrad Side Quest with a suggested level of 26. It's a murder mystery, with two key leads for Geralt to follow in
articles.body:
Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk is a Novigrad Side Quest with a suggested level of 26. It's a murder mystery, with two key leads for Geralt to follow in order to solve the crime and get to the bottom of what's causing the attacks in Oxenfurt.

Here's IGN's complete guide to Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk, including where to start the Side Quest and how to beat the combat encounter at the end.

To begin this Side Quest, head to Oxenfurt in the north of Velen, and look for the paper reading "Contract: Monster in Oxenfurt" as a starting point.

You'll need to find a character named Nikolas at the docks in Oxenfurt to learn more about the so-called monster, and the bodies that've been turning up in the gutter.

There are two leads for Geralt to follow with this Contract. You can speak to the witness, a lady who survived the attack, and speak to the medic caring for the bodies to examine them.

Talking to the witness, she sounds like a drunk lunatic, and she gets mad. Talking to the medic, he gets anxious about Geralt investigating the bodies. Examining the bodies, Geralt determines its a Vampire .

Head to where the monster was seen, and investigate using your Witcher senses. You'll discover a bracelet. Head back to the tavern, and get drunk to bait the Katakan. After getting drunk, Geralt will roam the streets singing drunk songs.

Eventually the Katakan emerges, and you will have to fight him, whilst drunk. Don't burn any combat items in this initial engagement, as you only need to take off a fourth of his health before he runs away -- focus on heavy attacks and dodging.

Follow the Katakan's trail using your Witcher Senses. The trail will lead to a house, which you can enter via a ladder. Finish off the Katakan, focusing on your movement in the enclosed area and watching for quick strikes. Don't be afraid to use additional items like Bombs here, either.

When you've beaten the beast, loot the corpse for a Katakan Trophy, the Deardgeith sword, a key to let you out of the locked house, and the Katakan Mutagen.

Return to the quest giver for your reward and to wrap up the Side Quest.

You'll receive your negotiated amount of money when turning in this Contract, along with 300 x experience, making it a worthwhile Contract to take on.

articles.title: Surprise! Facial recognition smart locks are actually good
articles.summary: We tested four facial recognition smart locks — the Eufy FamiLock E40, Lockly Visage Zeno, SwitchBot Lock Vision Pro, and Lockin Veno Solar Face — to find out which are worth buying.
articles.body: Hands-free unlocking is the future of smart locks. The best smart home tech removes friction, and having your door unlock for you as you walk up is as frictionless as it gets — no passcodes to remember, no need to have a free hand to wave, press, or poke at the lock. One way to achieve this nirvana is through facial recognition. You already unlock your phone with your face; why not your home? Hands-free unlocking using geofencing has been around for a while, but it can be slow and unreliable, and requires an app running in the background on your phone. Newer innovations — facial recognition and unlocking using an ultrawideband (UWB) radio — are much better. In my testing, UWB is the best experience. All it needs is your phone or watch somewhere on you to identify you as you approach, and it’s fast and reliable. But today, locks with UWB antennas are expensive, and very few are available. It was while reviewing one of them, the Schlage Sense Pro, that I discovered a genuine use case for facial recognition unlocking, a tech I had largely dismissed as an overengineered solution to a mostly solved problem. My husband often leaves his phone in the house when he’s working outside or in the garage, which means no hands-free unlocking for him. If you’re like him and don’t want an unlocking experience tied to a device, but want the speed and convenience of hands-free unlocking, facial unlocking may be for you. Facial recognition on smart locks uses infrared sensors to create a three-dimensional map of your face. Different companies use different methods — such as structured light, stereo infrared cameras, or time-of-flight sensing — but they’re all designed to do the same thing. The 3D part is key as it captures depth, so holding up a photo generally won’t fool them. I tested the four locks you can buy today with facial recognition unlocking — the $300 Eufy FamiLock E40, the $350 Lockly Visage Zeno, Lockin’s $199 Veno Solar Face, and Switchbot’s $230 Lock Vision Pro. There’s also one on Kickstarter that will launch next month, and Switchbot has a couple of variations. The facial recognition smart lock I would buy [Product: Eufy FamiLock E40 | The best of the bunch is the Eufy FamiLock E40 from Anker. If I’m going this high tech on my door, I’m going all the way, and the FamiLock E40 is a complete package. Along with excellent facial unlocking features, it also has a fingerprint reader, keypad, and a physical key, plus it doubles as a video doorbell. Stick this on your front door, and you are good to go. Of all four locks, the E40 was the fastest at unlocking using my face – it did it in under a second; I barely had to hesitate before opening. It is also the only one that worked consistently when I was wearing sunglasses. The rest did fine with hats, but struggled with sunglasses. The E40 also includes a backup battery that keeps the keypad active even if the main battery dies and biometrics don’t work — a nice touch. The lock portion supports the smart home standard Matter, so it can work in your ecosystem of choice, and viewing recorded footage from the built-in 2K video doorbell is subscription-free. I also appreciate that Eufy has added a touch of style to this lock; it looks more like a traditional lock than any of its competitors do. The downsides are that the Eufy is huge and expensive, and its lithium-ion battery takes nine hours to fully charge, though you can still use the lock while it’s charging. The main battery drains quickly; it dropped 40 percent in a week of testing. Overall, while expensive, the Eufy E40 offers a lot of value, looks good, and works well — as long as you’re willing to charge it regularly. There’s also a great option for Apple’s ecosystem [Product: Lockly Visage Zeno | My other favorite is the also-expensive Lockly Visage Zeno. This is the only lock that can do both Apple Home Key and facial recognition. Home Key is a nice backup when facial unlock is a tad too slow, since it’s super easy to tap your phone or watch to unlock it. If I’m in a hurry and my hands aren’t full, I just push my watch on it; otherwise, I let the facial scan do the work. The Lockly was slightly slower to unlock than the Eufy, taking about 2 seconds. It also struggled with sunglasses; it eventually unlocked, but took longer. The Lockly is also the oldest model I tested, launching in 2024. While it supports Home Key, it won’t work with Home Key UWB unlocking; it’s tap-to-unlock only. [Image: The keypad is designed to foil looky-loos, it also foiled my dad. I really like the style of the Lockly; it’s the sleekest and smallest, with the best build quality. Its battery life was impressive, lasting around nine months (I’ve been testing this lock for a year; the rest for a little over a week). It’s the only model that includes a spare battery, which helps with the sticker shock. However, it’s the most expensive lock I tested, and while facial recognition was good, its keypad is far too fiddly. Lockly’s PIN Genie system shuffles the digit layout every time you use it, and talking my dad through how to unlock it while I was trying to relax by a pool, and he was struggling to get into my house to feed my dog, was an exercise in frustration. Thankfully, there is now a version that lets you switch to a standard keypad layout. The category is still improving [Image: That is an emoji. On my door. The other two locks I tried have a lot of room for improvement, but they are also much less expensive. The main selling point of the Lockin Veno Solar Face is its built-in solar panel for extended battery life, and it worked well during my limited test period. But its facial unlocking was slower and didn’t work with sunglasses. This lock also has the worst addition I’ve ever seen on a smart lock — an animated emoji that dances when you unlock it. I could happily live the rest of my life without an emoji on my front door. [Product: Lockin Veno Solar Face | Lowest weather rating Animated emoji on your door Fewest unlocking methods] The SwitchBot Lock Vision Pro version was the worst of the bunch and glacially slow to unlock — I sometimes had to peer at the reader for several seconds before it would recognize me. Its fingerprint and palm-vein unlocking were more reliable, but it didn’t like sunglasses at all and kept seeing people who weren’t there. One night, I was sitting alone in my living room watching Widow’s Bay when the lock suddenly said, “Please stand closer to the door and try again.” I understandably freaked out, thinking someone was trying to get in. There was no one there, but it kept doing it. I eventually had to turn off sounds in the app to get it to stop. [Product: SwitchBot Lock Vision Pro | After trying these locks, I still think facial recognition is more tech than you need for your front door. Even if you don’t want to pay the premium for UWB, keypads and fingerprint readers work very well, are widely available, and are much less expensive. They are a touch slower, though, and do require you to use your hands. There are other tradeoffs for the speed and cool factor facial unlocking offers. Locks that support it aren’t as expensive as the current UWB locks, but they’re still pricey. And while there are more facial-recognition locks available than UWB locks, there still aren’t many. I also don’t think we’ll see many more once UWB, a simpler technology, takes off — something the new smart lock standard Aliro should help with. These locks also look unapologetically high tech and require you to get every member of your household to stand in front of the lock to register their face (I’m still trying to corral one of mine). Finally, not everyone will be comfortable storing their facial biometrics in a door lock, although for some it may feel more secure than using your phone as a key — only Nicolas Cage has successfully stolen someone’s face. The good news here is all the locks I tested claim to store and process data locally rather than in the cloud, which improves both privacy and performance. Facial recognition felt a bit weird at first, but it works and has that sci-fi cool factor. After living with both technologies, I prefer UWB. “Unlocking in stride” feels more magical because the door is already unlocked when I reach for the handle as opposed to waiting for a second or two for the lock to register that it’s me. But until more companies adopt UWB and prices come down, facial recognition is a good option for people who want hands-free unlocking today. Photos by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

A Court of Thorns and Roses (also known as ACOTAR) is a popular romantasy series that became a viral hit on #BookTok on TikTok. While an ACOTAR TV series was in the works at Hulu, it was scrapped in February 2025 . Still, two new books were announced by author Sarah J. Maas in March 2026 and are set to release in October 2026 and January 2027. Even without the TV adaptation, the series is moving beyond the pages of the book, expanding to tabletop games , jewelry, Funko Pop figures, and more.

The series’ publisher, Bloomsbury, has its own gift guide for ACOTAR and Maas’ other series, Throne of Glass and Crescent City, which are all connected via a multiverse (Maasverse). Additional official merchandise for ACOTAR can be found from sites, including Amazon, Target, and other online bookstores .

A Court of Thorns and Roses - Fate & Favor Board Game

An original strategy board game based on the books , called Fate & Favor, is available now. In the game, you play as either the High Lord or Lady of one of the seven Courts of Prythian as you forge alliances and fight for power. It’s full of familiar characters and scenes from the series, with event cards and shifting fate tokens, making things even more interesting. Created by true fans of ACOTAR, incredible detail is poured into everything from the gameplay to the artwork.

A Court of Thorn and Roses - Fate & Favor Booksellers Edition

A special “Bookseller Variant” with exclusive packaging at select bookstores can also be purchased.

Monopoly: A Court of Thorns and Roses Special Edition Board Game

Monopoly: A Court of Thorns and Roses Edition Board Game for Adults

Similar to Fourth Wing , ACOTAR has a Monopoly Edition. There's a classic red option to match the paperback cover of the first book and an Amazon-exclusive green variant. Rather than your typical locations, like Park Place and Boardwalk, the board highlights memorable places from the series. Golden tokens with items from the book, including Feyre's Bow and The Suriel, also replace the typical game pieces. This Monopoly even offers manors and palaces over houses and hotels.

Priorities: A Court of Thorns and Roses Edition Game

Also from Hasbro is A Court of Thorns and Roses Edition of Priorities. It's a party game where players must work together to correctly rank ACOTAR themed cards.

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: A Deck of Woulds or Rathers

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: FAE or Fraud?

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: Playing Card Set (Night Court Inner Circle)

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Fated Mates Pick-a-Stick: 50 Activities for Love & Romance

Several ACOTAR-themed card games are available or coming out, including a would-you-rather-type game, trivia, and a traditional deck of cards with characters from the Night Court. Another card-adjacent, adults-only activity provides prompts for a deeper connection with romantic partners.

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: Seven Courts of the Faerie Realm 1000-Piece Puzzle

A Court of Thorns & Roses Starfall 250-Piece Puzzle

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Mystery Mini Puzzle: Feyre’s Portraits

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: Greetings from Velaris 1000-Piece Puzzle

A Court of Thorns & Roses Walk Through The Rainbow 250 pcs Puzzle

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official A Tale of Fated Mates Rhysand and Feyre 1000-Piece Puzzle

A Court of Thorns & Roses Valkyrie Library Sleepover Keepsake 250 pcs Puzzle

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Still Life with Dread Trove 1000-Piece Puzzle

You can find puzzles that depict iconic scenes, characters, places, and more from the series at Amazon, Target, and other sites. For something more challenging, grab the 1,000-piece options, and for a quicker activity, there are a few 250-piece puzzles. A fun mystery box puzzle also reveals one of six character portraits.

Twitter Logo Save Funko POP! Feyre Under The Mountain

Popular characters from ACOTAR are now Funko Pop figures . Feyre has three different versions: her painting dresser drawers, her when she heads under the mountain, and her with a bow and arrow. Other figures include Tamlin in both beast form and masked, a masked Lucien, Rhysand, Amarantha, and The Suriel.

Based on the figures, this collection’s focus appears to be on the first book in the series.

A Court of Thorns and Roses Book Charms Locket Necklace

A Court of Thorns and Roses Book Covers Charm Toggle Bracelet

A Court of Thorns and Roses Bat Boys Ring Set of 3

A Court of Thorns and Roses Feyre Archeron Linear Bracelet

Alex and Ani has its own A Court of Thorns and Roses jewelry collection . Everything from a locket with adorable miniatures of the first five books to a charm bracelet that showcases the symbols and color palette of each book cover is available. You can even pick up one of the three bracelets inspired by the Archeron sisters, Feyre, Nesta, and Elain or Bat Boys rings. The collection is massive and looks incredible.

Youtooz ACOTAR Feyre Collectible Plush Figure, 9-Inch

Cuddle up with your favorite ACOTAR characters, as Youtooz has its own lineup of limited-edition plushies. These 9-inch plush figures are stuffed with 100% PP cotton and feature tons of details, from magical tattoos to a glittering wardrobe. There are five characters available: Rhysand, Feyre, Cassian, Azriel, and Nesta. Some are only preorders with shipping expected to begin in November.

A Court Of Thorns And Roses Take Me To The Night Court T-Shirt

A Court Of Wings & Ruins Only You Decide What Breaks You Throw Blanket

Tons of ACOTAR clothing is available from sites like Amazon and Etsy, but the best and biggest selection of officially licensed apparel and more is at Hot Topic and Target . Both have other collectibles that make great gifts, like pens, blankets, vases, totes, perfume, lights, and more. All are themed after the first five books, featuring memorable quotes, items, and places from the series. A few products are also available on Amazon via third-party sellers.

A Court of Thorns and Roses Hardcover Box Set

A Court of Thorns and Roses Paperback Box Set

A Court of Thorns and Roses Collector's Edition

ACOTAR is a popular audiobook and eBook series, but hardcover and paperback editions are great if you’d also like a physical copy to look back at. All five books currently released are available in those two formats, and books six and seven, whose covers and titles were recently announced , have hardcover copies for preorder . There’s also a hardcover and paperback box set of the first five books. A Collector’s Edition of the first book, the series’ namesake, A Court of Thorns and Roses, can even be found on Amazon.

Play-Doh Blooms A Court of Thorns and Roses

Play-Doh is now for adults too and is getting in on the ACOTAR brand with a new Blooms kit. The new kit comes with everything you need to build a bouquet and will release on January 15.

articles.title: The Best Places to Buy LEGO Sets in 2026
articles.summary: Here's where you should be buying your bricks.
articles.body:
Over the past decade, the popularity and demand for LEGO has soared. What was once a building toy for children has expanded its audience to include teens and adults . And the sets themselves have expanded in detail, utility, and variance.

Some sets are built for play. Others are built for display, as dioramas or expensive collectibles. And a growing number of sets are lifestyle accessories – wall decorations , plants, and flowers – that integrate themselves into the living space.

There are hundreds of LEGO sets currently available for purchase, across a wide variety of piece counts, themes, and prices. And interested buyers might run into two primary problems: not finding the set they want, and if they do, not finding it at a reasonable price.

The most common reason for either problem is that the specific set is "retired." LEGO retires all its sets – even its popular ones – to make room for new ones. And this has created a rampant resell culture, in which merchants mark up their inventory up to 2-3 times their original price.

It's also a hard reality that LEGO is expensive , period, and has been getting more so for the past several years. Take, for example, the massive, 7,541-piece Star Wars Millennium Falcon that launched in 2017. At the time, it cost $800, which was already well above the typical '10 cents per piece' rate of most sets. Today, that same set costs $850. LEGO topped itself with the LEGO Death Star that costs a whopping $1,000.

You can alleviate these problems by being a smart, meticulous consumer. Here are the best places to shop for LEGO sets in 2026, along with the best times to look for deals.

The first, most obvious place to shop for LEGO online is the official LEGO Store, which has the widest selection available and is easily sortable by theme, price, release date, and customer rating. LEGO has responsive customer service as well as a LEGO Insiders program . It's free to sign up, and it comes with numerous perks.

You can buy sets before they launch to the general public. You can receive free sets as incentives for spending money. And there are several sets that are exclusive to the LEGO Store , which cannot be bought from a third-party retailer.

The most appealing aspect of the LEGO Store is its point system . Every dollar you spend converts to 6.5 points. 130 points is the equivalent of $1. That works out to 5% of whatever money you put into the system, which you save up and redeem towards a future purchase.

There are also specific times during the year where you can earn double the points, which maximizes the program's value. More on that later.

Your other best online options are Amazon, Best Buy, Target and Walmart. While they do not have the point system or the exclusivity of the official store, they offer modest discounts for most of their sets, and oftentimes have sets in stock when LEGO.com runs out. The LEGO Store, meanwhile, typically charges full retail price except on select occasions, like when it's trying to get rid of inventory near the end of a set's run.

Thus, it becomes a matter of weighing your options. Would you rather wait for a set to go on sale somewhere else, or would you rather pay full retail price at the online LEGO Store, but receive a future discount and an exclusive small set for free? For brand new sets , this makes the LEGO Store the best place to shop almost every time.

Lastly, there are the unofficial online marketplaces on Craigslist, eBay, Facebook, and more. If you're looking for a retired set, this is your only option, and be warned: your acquisition will come at a steep price. Definitely get in touch with the seller directly, be ready to haggle, and shop around to get the best possible deal. There are usually some retired LEGO sets still available on Amazon shortly after LEGO officially sunsets them, but the prices tend to go up over time.

Brick-and-mortar stores are your other option. It is unlikely you'll find a wider diversity of LEGO sets in person than you would online, but many people prefer personalized attention and want to physically handle a set before purchasing it.

The in-person LEGO Store is a great choice for the same reasons that the online LEGO Store is a great choice. The LEGO Insiders program and its point system carry over to either option. LEGO Stores also provide interactive fun. They often contain a LEGO building station and a LEGO minifigure station, where you can choose from hundreds of body parts and accessories to create your own Mini-Me.

Target and Walmart have dedicated LEGO sections in their stores, and again, should be evaluated against the LEGO Store's inventory on a case-by-case basis. Gamestop occasionally sells gaming-themed LEGO sets. It is unlikely that smaller outlets will be offering discounts, but it doesn't hurt to look

For the LEGO gift giver and casual shoppers:

Best Buy also has many popular LEGO sets in-store like Pokémon, Star Wars and Disney LEGO, but may be limited to smaller sets and inventory varies by location. Barnes and Noble sells LEGO as well: lifestyle sets, impulse purchase smaller sets, and Harry Potter sets (which makes sense, since Harry Potter is one of the best selling book franchises in history).

Aside from regular discounts at the box-stores (which are the baseline default, rather than the exception), LEGO sets rarely receive discounts. The demand is high, and LEGO would rather retire a set than discount it. But there are specific times of the year when LEGO sets go on sale to watch out for.

LEGO typically celebrates May 4 (Star Wars Day) by offering double the Insider points for purchasing Star Wars sets . LEGO also celebrates March 10 (Mario Day) by partnering with Nintendo and offering similar deals. So watch out for notable anniversaries, particularly as they relate to 3rd party franchises.

Always look for clearance deals at the box-stores, which are more common at the beginning of the year. That's when LEGO retires scores of old sets and launches scores of new sets. This requires the 3rd party retailers to refresh their inventory.

Lastly, the holiday season is ideal for deep discounts, particularly on Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Amazon Prime Days, which run in July and October, are also solid opportunities. Keep an eye out for any upcoming sales events for potential LEGO deals.

Kevin Wong is a contributing freelancer for IGN, specializing in LEGO. He's also been published in Complex, Engadget, Gamespot, Kotaku, and more. Follow him on Twitter at @kevinjameswong .

articles.body:
Forge Weaponry or Armor is an early game quest given to you by Oswald the Blacksmith . It's one of the first quests you'll get, but it's also one of the most important. Learning how to craft is essential in Enshrouded , and if you're stuck, we are here to walk you through it.

To get started, you first need to save the Blacksmith by completing the Find the Sleeping Survivor quest. Once Oswald is set up in your base, talk to him to learn more about crafting. He will give you the Forge Weaponry or Armor quest around this point.

To complete the quest, you need to craft any weapon or piece of armor available to you. The easiest thing to go for is a weapon, such as the Daggers. All you need to craft those is 4x Scrap Metal . You can find this in and around ruins, but the most efficient way to collect it is by defeating and looting Scavengers. There are plenty of Scavengers throughout every region in Enshrouded, but in this case, you should head to Rookmore .

If Daggers aren't your style, you could also craft a Wand out of 2x Bones . Bones are just as plentiful, if not more-so, than Metal Scaps in the early game. You can find some by looting skeletons and defeating enemies like Wolves. There are lots of those in the Springlands!

Once you've completed your excursion to Rookmore, head back to base and craft any weapon or piece of armor to complete the quest!

articles.title: Dead by Daylight Developer Apologizes Again, Removes Free Items From TheBurntPeanut's Account
articles.summary: Behavior Interactive is currently under fire after one of its community staff allegedly went rogue and gifted controversial streamer TheBurntPeanut every in-game item in Dead by Daylight live on stream. The developer already apologized once on the secondary Dead by Daylight social media account, but this latest mea culpa, in an attempt to take full accountability, was posted on the full-fat account.
articles.body:
Behavior Interactive is currently under fire after one of its community staff allegedly went rogue and gifted controversial streamer TheBurntPeanut every in-game item in Dead by Daylight live on stream. The developer already apologized once on the secondary Dead by Daylight social media account, but this latest mea culpa, in an attempt to take full accountability, was posted on the full-fat account.

TheBurntPeanut gained popularity over the last year for playing extraction shooters like Arc Raiders, but his style of commentary is seen as edgy by some and problematic by others. Earlier this year, Fortnite was wrapped up in similar drama for collaborating with TheBurntPeanut due to accusations he’d allegedly used homophobic language online.

Dead by Daylight 10th Anniversary Broadcast Visual Overhaul Reveal - Screenshots

Dead by Daylight initially starts players with a small selection of playable characters, but they must spend in-game currency to earn the rest, while licensed characters cost around $5 in real money. Gifting TheBurntPeanut all the characters was taken as a betrayal by the community, which has many dedicated streamers who haven’t been gifted everything the game has to offer.

Not only was his alleged behavior never taken into account, but it sparked favoritism concerns considering it was the first time the streamer had shown an interest in Dead by Daylight. Initially, TheBurntPeanut offered to send the freebies back, concerned that it would cause drama. Responding to the online outrage, the studio reportedly sent support TheBurntPeanut's way, with the most infamous message saying, "WE CAN TAKE THE HEAT! THEY ARE YOURS TO KEEP!"

A video from seven months ago shows the streamer saying he doesn’t understand the game’s popularity. “No disrespect, but how the hell has a game where you fix four generators and then leave, rinse and repeat, been alive for ten years?” he said.

The streamer himself has since responded to the controversy, which bubbled away on social media between the weekend and today. “I just went on Twitter for a second and everyone’s pissed at us for getting free skins in Dead by Daylight,” TheBurntPeanut said in a recent video . “There’s one guy that’s submitted a refund, and in the refund reason box they go, ‘TheBurntPeanut collaboration and the response of the game’s communication team — I do not support racist transphobes.’

“I don’t think I’ve ever said anything about transgender people, I think, in the last two-and-a-half years of streaming. Have I ever said anything about transgender people?” He asked this question to another streamer, who replied: “I don’t think so, but there’s always time to start.” This made TheBurntPeanut start laughing. “Where are they getting this from?” he asked. He didn’t address the racism accusations.

Behavior Interactive’s new apology , posted on the main account, claimed that it will put in new approval processes to prevent community representatives from being able to choose who Dead by Daylight collaborates with without checks.

Explaining the initial decision to grant TheBurntPeanut an unlocked account, the latest apology claimed that the team saw a new streamer with a large audience playing the game and got excited at the prospect of reaching new players. But the decision to grant the account perks happened without any internal discussion.

“When collaborating with a new creator, we normally look thoroughly at their past content to determine whether they are representing the values of inclusion our community expects from us,” Behaviour explained. “In this case, this was not taken into proper consideration or discussed as a group.”

The studio also spoke about the infamous “WE CAN TAKE THE HEAT” message. “This message, along with some others in that session, showed a disregard for the context we were suddenly in and crossed the line of appropriate responses from our brand,” the statement continued. “That reply escalated the situation for us and for our community, especially our content creators on the frontlines of these conversations, and that’s unacceptable.”

According to the developer, the account bonuses have already been removed from TheBurntPeanut, and Behavior is rewriting its guidelines for interacting with creators and identifying potentially problematic collaborations. The studio is “taking appropriate action internally” to deal with the employee involved, but the details of this will remain confidential.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: What Does Sentinel Mean? Are Giant Robots Involved? The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Lore Explained
articles.summary: What does Sentinel mean? How is it connected to Skyrim? Are we getting giant robots? Here's a deep dive lore explainer on The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel.
articles.body:
The worst-kept secret in gaming has finally been confirmed: yes, The Elder Scrolls 6 has a title. It’s called Sentinel, and will take place in Hammerfell, the province of northwest Tamriel previously featured in Daggerfall and Elder Scrolls Online (also Arena, but anyone who says they played that recently is lying). The point is, more than any previous mainline entry in the Elder Scrolls series, Sentinel will be depicting a fairly well-trodden location. But given its geographical location and significance in The Lore, I think there’s a fairly good chance that TES 6 will feature two distinct elements: ships and giant robots. Stay with me on this.

So what is Sentinel? Well, it’s a city and kingdom – think New York, New York – on the southern shores of the Iliac Bay, the northern edge of Hammerfell province, stretching from the Alik'r Desert and coastal regions in the west to the Dragontail Mountains in the east.

It’s a hugely important maritime city in Tamrielic lore, being the founding settlement of the Redguards. Its geography and architecture are heavily inspired by North Africa and the Middle East: the city of Sentinel is often depicted almost like classical Baghdad, with its beautiful domed palace and spires in the centre, river canals lined with palm trees, and sandblasted common districts full of markets and street vendors. It is one of the preeminent locations of TheElder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall, second only perhaps to Daggerfall itself, its opposite number and historical rival across the water. Like Rome and Carthage squabbling over Sicily, Sentinel and Daggerfall’s shared past mostly pivots around a dispute over the island of Betony, a strategically significant fishing community off the coast of High Rock which used to be a protectorate of Sentinel until Daggerfall decided to sink their navy over it.

It’s a region rich with naval tradition, arguably with lots of parallels to the Mediterranean. The northern province of High Rock may be taken as a composite of Latin and Germanic Europe as a counterpart to Sentinel’s obvious riffs on the Arab-descended Moorish people who once colonised the Iberian Peninsula. Which is fitting, because if Elder Scrolls is anything, it’s extremely moreish.

What’s important is that the Iliac Bay is full of tiny islands. The lore is steeped in boat stuff. The Redguards themselves are a seafaring people in the same way that Bretons are a magic one, or that the Imperials are really good at accountancy: it’s at the heart of their culture, their DNA. Which, given that Sentinel is named for their home nation, would seem to track with the rumour from several billion years ago that The Elder Scrolls 6 would feature, or at least was once intended to feature, some sort of ship-based component. That could mean anything or nothing, of course, but if every Elder Scrolls game is to be its own proposition, then this would certainly be a defining trope for the new one. Skyrim had dragons. Oblivion had portals to hell. Morrowind had big mushrooms. Yum.

Beyond the bay itself, we have the fallen continent of Yokuda, where the Redguards originally hail from, and the large island nation of Stros M’Kai, the setting of Bethesda’s one-time experiment in doing a third-person adventure spin-off of the Elder Scrolls. The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard wasn’t a huge success in itself, but it did teach the studio a great deal about the relationship between scale and hand-crafted detail that resulted in a massive difference in approach between Daggerfall and Morrowind. Where the former boasted a map twice the size of the UK, Morrowind crammed infinitely more intrigue into a region barely a full percentage of the size, brought the series to consoles, and subsequently made the studio a household name.

Bethesda would stick to this philosophy of staunchly hand-crafted worlds until Starfield, which depicted a thousand-planet galaxy of endless walking, pocked with procedurally generated identikit outposts and very little incentive to go off the laid-out path, which many would argue – myself included, and I like Starfield – betrayed a studio that had lost touch with its core appeal. But think of the parts of Starfield which are successful, at least as a proof of concept: a mobile home in the form of a starship, to which you can assign crew, and go adventuring with them. A hugely popular ship builder that simplified the process of pimping your ride down to a snap-together kitbash, that allowed for enormous creativity within a deceptively rigid framework.

It’s not a given that any of this will be relevant to Sentinel, or that if any of these systems carried over they would retain their complexity. But it does demonstrate that, if TES 6 were to think about this sort of direction, it’s hardly unprecedented at this point.

What’s also not unprecedented in Bethesda’s oeuvre is kaiju. Big bastards smashing the gaffe up. Some years before Fallout 3’s Liberty Prime made us all piss ourselves unintentionally, the end of Oblivion depicted daedric prince Mehrunes Dagon ransacking the Imperial City, and you’ll probably remember that he’s a big dude, so big that he could only be seen off by the literal embodiment of Akatosh as a nine-storey dragon. And yes, the dragons of Skyrim qualify: the entire game being built around the proposition of seeing off a veritable invasion of enormous, scaly bastards. And Morrowind before them was all about preventing Dagoth Ur from building a second Numidium with which to conquer the world: a gigantic Dwarven mech powered by the literal heart of a god, based on the schematics of a weapon of mass destruction that was once used by the city-state of Sentinel to conquer the rest of the region.

And there’s a whole other bunch of stuff that happened: if you want to know more, boot up Morrowind, or Oblivion, or Skyrim, and read an in-game book entitled The Warp in the West, which explains a convoluted collision of realities in which every rival faction got to use Numidium to get their preferred Daggerfall ending, making all of them canon at once. Which you might call a cop-out, but it certainly neatly solves the kinds of insurmountable issues that crop up when you try to respect all player choices.

The point is this: after the events of Daggerfall, Numidium is destroyed, and pieces of it are scattered all over Hammerfell and High Rock. Perhaps some of it sank to the bottom of the bay. Perhaps some of it is buried in the desert. The quote displayed at the end of the recent Sentinel teaser talks about the experience of Yazar, a Moth Priest, trying to interpret a prophecy from one of the Elder Scrolls and receiving only a faint image of some kind of terrible future. Or past. Or parallel present. “A future lost, a victory undone, sands of time scattered by fate”.

Like much of Elder Scrolls lore, it is esoteric and steeped in double-meaning. As a region at the heart of the Warp in the West, the ‘sands of time’ could well refer literally to the Alik'r Desert while caught in a time-warp. A ‘victory undone’ may refer to any number of conflicts referenced in the series’ history, but the most pertinent one would seem to be Sentinel’s “victory” at the end of Daggerfall, in which it became the capital of a vast coastal region as the various bickering city-states and territories were consolidated into the four currently standing kingdoms of the Iliac Bay, which, along with Sentinel, includes the Breton kingdoms of Daggerfall and Wayrest, and the Orcish kingdom of Orsinium.

To undo the victory could mean to scatter these territories back to their fragments. Or, it could refer to the events preceding the last Elder Scrolls game, Skyrim, where the empire of Tamriel finds itself in a precarious peace with the treacherous Aldmeri Dominion after decades of brutal war, following the treaty known as the White Gold Concordat. This stipulated, firstly, the criminalisation of Talos worship, which much of Skyrim’s civil war arc is concerned with. Secondly, the disbanding of the Blades, the emperor’s secret service. And lastly, the cession of southern Hammerfell to the High Elves. You can imagine this didn’t go down especially well with the Redguards of Sentinel, which is why they left the Empire shortly afterward.

It’s not a huge stretch to assume that Sentinel will continue the story of this conflict, with the Aldmeri Dominion an occupying army in regions of Hammerfell that the player may be tasked with liberating. Or, perhaps we will be enrolled in an effort to construct a weapon with which to decisively end the war. Say, a giant dwarven mech. Reassembling the pieces of Numidium left by the warp in the west would seem to be a classic motivation for RPG storytelling. And it would be especially fitting to use against the High Elves. Numidium itself is a construct of the ancient Dwarves that has been used in a number of pivotal wars. Most notably, it was used by the founding emperor Tiber Septim to bring the Aldmeri to heel on Summerset Isle: a weapon of mass destruction set loose onto the entire civilian population, an incident which is largely credited with inspiring the general disdain High Elves have for the human races, and the Imperials in particular.

Numidium is an offensive cultural trauma for the Aldmeri Dominion. It represents the moment when they lost their sovereignty to the Empire, a subjugation that would last right up until the end of the Oblivion Crisis. The colossal machine is depicted in the Wall of Alduin in Skyrim, a part of the Dragonborn prophecy that is concerned with the warping of time which, according to the UESP, is an effect that occurs along with every known use of Numidium in history.

But what could power such a construct, in a world of candlelight and shit dinners? Well, the literal heart of a God. In Morrowind, the player character thwarts the building of a second Numidium by destroying the Heart of Lorkhan, or the Heart of the Red Mountain, one of the most important objects in the entire Elder Scrolls universe, perhaps even more important than the manuscripts themselves.

Sentinel is rumoured to be, at long last, concerned with the origins of the titular scrolls: these objects of divine prophecy that have shown up throughout the series but have never been fully understood. They are cared for by the Moth Priests, a sect of blind scholars whose work in interpreting the scrolls robs them of their sight; such is the retina-searing power of creation they are believed to hold. They are said to be byproducts of the creation of the universe, fragments of time, space, and everything. Star stuff. God particles. The celestial parchment on which is written the underlying code of existence. And Lorkhan, the missing god whose heart is required to power Numidium, was there at their creation, having tricked the god Mundus into creating the Elder Scrolls universe in the first place.

The Elder Scrolls 6 is likely the culmination of an enormous tapestry of imagined history that goes right back to Daggerfall, and deeply involves every single Elder Scrolls protagonist thereafter. Tracing the Heart of Lorkhan and the pieces of Numidium through history until, perhaps, their final reassembly in the war against Sentinel and the Aldmeri Dominion. And where is Lorkhan said to have died? At the Adamantine Tower, on the island of Balferia in the Iliac Bay. Perhaps something remains of him there that we will have to recover. Maybe we’ll end up flying to one of the moons in a big dwarven rocket to recover one of Lorkhan’s toes. I don’t know. But I’d love to do it. The upshot? The Elder Scrolls 6 is going to be absolutely stacked to the gills with tidbits for sickos. And I can’t wait to play it in 2038.

articles.title: The Cat in the Hat Animated Adaptation Features Bill Hader as the Whimsical Dr. Seuss Character
articles.summary: The Cat in the Hat (2026) review: The whimsical Dr. Seuss character gets a good but not great animated feature film showcase.
articles.body:
The Cat in the Hat is in theaters on on November 6.

Having received a 2003 live-action adaptation that left much to be desired , the Cat in the Hat is back with a new feature film. This time, it’s in animated form, and fortunately the end result is a much better one.

With Mike Myers having starred in the live-action version, another group of filmmakers have once more turned to a Saturday Night Live alum, with Bill Hader now voicing the Cat. Dr. Seuss's beloved children's book is far too short to make for a feature-length story on its own, so things are rather drastically reinterpreted and expanded upon here, with writer-directors Erica Rivinoja (South Park, Borat Subsequent Moviefilm) and Alessandro Carloni (Kung Fu Panda 3) essentially just taking the basic idea of the fantastical Cat in the Hat appearing to children to encourage imagination and mischief.

The opening scenes feel somewhat similar to Monsters, Inc., establishing an entire imagination-based business of sorts with the Cat in the Hat as an employee. Other anthropomorphic animals work alongside him, all in the service of providing entertainment and encouragement to kids needing an imagination boost. Fortunately, the film doesn’t get too bogged down in the “company” scenario, mostly using it as a fun way to incorporate nods to the Seuss-y source material in the form of rhyming rules explained by staff members (voiced by the likes of Giancarlo Esposito, Bowen Yang, and Quinta Brunson), along with some visual depictions of the Cat in that Hat that also harken back to the book. From there, the story follows the Cat appearing to sister and brother Gabby (Xochitl Gomez) and Sebastian (Tiago Martinez), who are trying to deal with moving to a new city with their mother, Carmen (America Ferrera).

The Cat in the Hat shows genuine creativity from the start, beginning with its distinct visual interpretation of its two worlds. The realm the Cat and his colleagues live in appears much more bright, colorful, and off-kilter compared to the more realistic and muted feel given to Gabby and Sebastian’s apartment life. The film thankfully provides solid laughs on a fairly frequent basis too, from sight gags and slapstick that can entertain all ages to some notably multilayered jokes that can easily work for kids but arguably hit harder for the adults in the audience.

It also certainly helps to have Bill Hader voicing the Cat, bringing his deft sense of humor to the role along with his ability to do impressive voices. In addition to Hader, the movie has a bit of a cheat code in the form of Matt Berry (What We Do in the Shadows) as the voice of Gabby and Sebastian's pet fish, Waffles, who the Cat promptly gives the ability to speak. Is there a greater and more innately funny voice than Berry's these days? Hearing his bombastic delivery as an overwhelmed and frustrated fish is continually funny.

The film’s storyline involves the Cat introducing and then promptly losing a device that functions in a manner similar to Doctor Strange's Time Stone, enabling the user to rewind recent events. The search for this device takes the Cat, Gabby, and Sebastian inside incredible versions of the moving boxes that still fill the kids’ apartment; they travel through worlds where everything inside these boxes appears larger than life, often having actually come to life in the form of various toys, objects, and drawings they encounter. While some of this is a bit reminiscent of the journey through the mind in Inside Out, there are a lot of unique and appreciated touches throughout as everything from musical instruments to IKEA instructions can and do express themselves in various ways.

The one big drawback with the film is that it’s simply too long for its subject matter, losing energy as it nears its conclusion. Running just a few minutes shy of two hours, it starts to drag in its third act; an obvious reason for this is that there are just too many overlapping conflicts introduced. The film is ultimately juggling the Cat’s quest to get back his lost device; a monstrous creature called “Something” who is pursuing our heroes; the fact that the Cat in the Hat's job is in jeopardy thanks to recent screw-ups; and another subplot about Carmen’s snooping landlord (Paula Pell), who is itching for a reason to evict the new family in the building thanks to her strict rules. It feels like Rivinoja and Carloni overcompensated for how slight the book is; the movie would have been better served by dropping at least one of these storylines, as the movie feels noticeably stretched out as it nears its resolution.

Still, despite overstaying its welcome, The Cat in the Hat remains easy to enjoy thanks to its likability and humor. That includes how it makes use of the book’s popular Thing 1 and Thing 2 characters, who are expanded here into a large group of similar Thing creatures that the Cat unleashes into Gabby and Sebastian’s apartment. These weird little guys have an amusing and wacky Gremlins-type chaotic energy, even as you can feel the studio salivating at the chance to turn the Things into the next Minions. But being aware of that is made easier when you’re watching an often sly film like The Cat in the Hat, which provides its own very good meta joke that acknowledges this fact with a wink.

articles.title: Maxroll’s World of Warcraft: Forever Guides
articles.body:
World of Warcraft: Forever launches on November 4, and Maxroll has prepared a new branch of guides and tools to help players get started. As IGN’s Game Help Alliance partner for RPGs, Maxroll brings its class and build expertise to the new version of Azeroth, with class guides, tier lists, and tools to help players plan their characters. Here's what you can find on Maxroll.

Maxroll’s class guides cover all nine classes , with leveling builds and advice on talents, rotations, gear, professions, and getting around Azeroth. Each guide is designed to help players understand their class as they level and make decisions about how to play.

Browse the Class Guides , or jump straight to a class:

Use Maxroll’s Planner to plan your build and try out different talent choices with the talent calculator. Once you have a build in mind, you can share it with friends or export it for your character.

You can also browse Community Builds to see how other players have set up their characters. These builds can give you ideas or act as a starting point for your own setup.

If you haven’t decided which class to play, Maxroll’s Tier Lists can help you compare your options. They include rankings for solo and group leveling, along with separate lists for DPS , tank , and healer roles .

The WoW Forever news section is where you can catch up on the latest updates and announcements. Check back as the game develops to see what’s changing and what’s coming next.

The branch is just getting started. Maxroll plans to add more guides, including in-depth endgame guides and class guides for max-level content, as players move beyond leveling and take on the challenges ahead.

A full database is also planned, where players will be able to look up items, talents, and skills. It will give players a place to find details on the things they encounter and use throughout their adventures.

Visit the Maxroll WoW Forever homepage to explore the branch.
